title: Per Cent Grid
description: Shade a hundred grid, read the shading as a fraction over 100 and as a per cent, and fold the grid into a strip of ten equal cells.
modes: none. One flow, one phase at a time. The host mounts a phase (phase prop). With navigableDots true, or no phase, the child may jump phases with the dots (user mode); otherwise the dots show progress and the teacher agent drives window.toolApi (AI mode). The last phase, and a whole lesson, end on the summary page, where Free play and Play again sit. With navDots the dots are controls in AI mode too: a tap on a dot starts that phase.

stage.sizing: the frame is min(100vw, 177.78vh) wide and min(100vh, 56.25vw) tall (dvh where supported); the svg fills it. Nothing scrolls.

bands.header: 0 to 80. One line: the tool name, a measured dot, the phase concept; Hint, sound and restart as round controls far right.
bands.canvas: 92 to 640. One rounded card holding the key at its top right (Answer, Close, Enter, Next, or the Yes / No keys; no question bar), the working area (the whole card until Answer is tapped) and the answer drawer that slides in from the right; the summary page covers it at the end.
bands.footer: 652 to 900. The mascot at the far left on its ground line, the speech bubble beside it (y 656 to 892, the question and every line, printed), one small dot per phase at the right.

zones.layout: board, key only: no question bar, only its key at the right end of the top row (the question is on the bubble); the working area is the whole card (64, 108, 1472 x 520) until the child taps Answer, when the answer drawer (as tall as the working area, the key on its top row reading Close) slides in from the right
zones.controls: circles r 28 at cx 1388, 1460, 1532, cy 40: Hint (data-control again), sound, restart; 72-unit finger boxes
zones.dots: one small dot per phase at the footer's right (72-unit finger boxes, centred on the bubble), no text; in user AND AI mode each is a button (data-control phase-dot, data-phase k) that starts its phase

stage.noSidebar: There is no sidebar. The canvas takes every unit the chrome can spare.
stage.noScoreBox: There is no score box on the stage. The score leaves on finished and onComplete and is shown once, as stars on the summary page.

writeup.why: Read and shade a per cent on a hundred grid as a count out of a hundred, write it as a fraction over 100 and with the % sign, and see a strip of ten equal cells as the same whole in columns.
writeup.look: A full ten by ten grid at the left, the Columns and cells counter under it, a fraction card and a per cent card at its right, and on the last phase a strip of ten equal cells.
writeup.stage: Three bands across 1600 by 900. The header runs 0 to 80 and is one line only: 'Per Cent Grid' in ink at the far left, a small dot set clear of the name, the phase title beside the dot on the same line, the host's navigation, and sound and restart as three round controls at the far right. The canvas runs 92 to 746, one rounded card on the paper colour. At its top left, at x 64, y 108 and 330 by 76, sits the running count: how many cells are shaded, out of one hundred. It is never a score. The working area is 1086 by 528 at x 64, y 202. The grid is 480 by 480 with its top left at x 110, y 230, ruled into ten columns and ten rows of equal cells in near-black and labelled Whole and 100% above it. Shaded cells are deep blue and unshaded cells stay warm white. The Columns and cells counter stands at x 640, y 240, reading the shading in words as full columns and single cells. The fraction card and the per cent card stand one above the other at x 640, y 360 and x 640, y 480, each 300 by 90, and turn green when the child's answer matches the shading. The Scatter and Fold buttons sit side by side at x 640, y 620, each labelled in words. On the fourth phase the ten columns close up into a strip 900 long and 80 tall at x 110, y 420, each of its ten equal cells labelled one tenth, the shaded columns becoming shaded cells. Down the right of the canvas, in the same rectangle on every phase and never animated in or out, the question sits above the answer slot at x 1186, y 250 (356 by 92) that holds what the child has given, and under it the pad at x 1170, y 368 (388 by 363). The pad is ten number keys with a fraction bar key and a % key, for setting a count of cells up to one hundred, or typing a fraction or a per cent into the answer slot. The footer runs 758 to 900: the voice caption at the far left with its speaking dot beside it, measuring its own wrap and dropping a type size rather than spilling, and the phase bar at the right with the question count under it. There is no sidebar and no score box anywhere, and nothing is ever written over the working area. Content colours are the chapter's own, and the tools of this chapter share them. The part the question gives, as shaded cells, a fraction, a decimal or an amount, is deep blue, labelled Given. The per cent, fraction or decimal the working reaches, and what is left after a part is used, is green, labelled Answer or Left. Both terms multiplied or divided by one number, and the times one hundred step before the % sign, are vermilion, labelled Both terms or Times 100. A unit fact that puts two amounts in one unit is violet, labelled Unit fact. The part used, taken away or not won is rose, labelled Used or Not won. The step, cell or number being worked on now is amber. A zero holding a place open inside a decimal is grey, labelled Place holder, and nothing else on the stage is ever grey. An unshaded cell of a whole stays warm white inside its near-black outline, the % sign is near-black ink, and anything dimmed fades to half strength rather than turning grey. Chrome never borrows one of them, and each reading survives with the colour taken away, because a part is told by its written label before it is told by its colour.
writeup.finish: The cards show the last shading as a fraction over 100 and as a per cent, with the grid and its folded strip side by side.

phases.win: the fraction card reads 53/100 and the per cent card 53%, both green
phases.does: counts the full columns, then the single cells, and types the count over one hundred
phases.goal: a number of shaded cells out of the 100 cells of a hundred grid is that many per cent
phases.says: A hundred equal cells. Count the shaded ones. How many out of a hundred?
phases.check: Away from the screen: a hundred children are in a hall, and some wear red. How would you say that part as a per cent?
phases.feels: the count out of a hundred turning into a per cent in one step
phases.hands: Draw a ten by ten grid on squared paper, shade some full columns and a few more cells, and write the count over one hundred and again with the % sign.
phases.tries: First rung: count the full columns only. Second rung: count the single cells only. Third rung: the same task with fewer full columns shaded, before the full shading returns.

wrong.why: both kinds of cell are right there, and the white ones can look like the part asked about
wrong.move: counts the unshaded cells instead of the shaded ones
wrong.screen: each shaded cell gets a small number in turn, column by column, and the unshaded cells stay warm white and unnumbered

wrong.why: a column looks like one long thing, so it feels like one
wrong.move: counts each full column as one cell
wrong.screen: each full column lights amber in turn with its ten cells numbered down it, and the counter adds ten for it

phases.screen: a grid with five full columns and three more cells shaded, and the cards blank
phases.soWhat: per cent means out of a hundred
phases.concept: Per cent means out of a hundred

phases.win: three columns and one cell shaded, and the per cent card reads 31%
phases.does: shades as many cells as the numerator says, and types the per cent
phases.goal: a fraction over 100 is written as a per cent by its numerator, with the % sign
phases.says: The bottom number is already a hundred. The top number is the per cent.
phases.check: Away from the screen: what is the same about forty-seven out of a hundred and forty-seven per cent?
phases.feels: the fraction card and the per cent card saying the same number
phases.hands: Write a fraction over one hundred on a card, shade that many cells of a paper grid, and write the numerator with the % sign beside it.
phases.tries: First rung: read the bottom number and check it is one hundred. Second rung: read the top number aloud. Third rung: the same task with a numerator under ten, before the full fraction returns.

wrong.why: the number is right, so the sign seems like decoration
wrong.move: types the numerator with no % sign
wrong.screen: the grid's count is written under it with the word hundredths, and the empty place after the child's number in the answer slot is lit amber

wrong.why: one hundred is the biggest number on the card

phases.screen: the question card showing 31/100 and an empty grid
phases.soWhat: the numerator of a fraction over one hundred is the per cent

phases.win: the cells are scattered to new places, and the per cent card still reads 27%
phases.does: shades full columns first, then single cells, then taps Scatter and watches the cards
phases.goal: any cells of the right count show a per cent, full columns of ten first
phases.says: Shade the right number of cells. Does it matter which ones?
phases.check: Away from the screen: two friends shade the same per cent, one in columns and one scattered. How could you check both?
phases.feels: the cells scattering across the grid while the per cent card holds still
phases.hands: Shade the asked number of cells anywhere on a paper grid. Swap grids with a partner, and count each other's shading column by column.
phases.tries: First rung: shade the full columns only. Second rung: add the single cells one at a time. Third rung: the same task with a per cent under ten, before the full count returns.

wrong.why: both digits are counts, and the first one read gets used first
wrong.move: swaps the tens and the ones, shading the ones digit as full columns
wrong.screen: the shaded columns are numbered ten, twenty and on in amber, and the question's per cent is written beside the running count so the two are read together

wrong.why: every grid the child has seen shades tidy columns

phases.screen: an empty grid and the question card asking for 27%
phases.soWhat: any cells of the right count show a per cent, full columns of ten first

phases.win: four cells shaded, and the per cent card reads 40% under the words four tenths
phases.does: taps Fold, counts the cells of the strip, and shades some of them
phases.goal: a strip of ten equal cells is the whole, and each cell is ten hundredths of it
phases.says: Ten columns fold into ten equal cells. What per cent is one cell?
phases.check: Away from the screen: if every cell of a strip of ten is shaded, what per cent is shaded?
phases.feels: a whole grid folding into ten wide cells
phases.hands: Fold a paper grid along its column lines into a strip of ten, colour some of the strip's cells, and say each cell as ten per cent.
phases.tries: First rung: shade one cell of the strip and read the card. Second rung: shade one more and read it again. Third rung: the same task with the grid opened out beside the strip.

wrong.why: on the grid one cell was one per cent, so the habit carries over
wrong.move: counts each cell of the strip as one per cent
wrong.screen: Fold runs back once, the grid opening out so each strip cell is seen to cover a whole column of ten, then it closes again

wrong.why: the white cells are just as easy to count
wrong.move: counts the unshaded cells of the strip

phases.screen: the grid with its ten columns outlined in amber and the Fold button lit
phases.soWhat: a strip of ten equal cells is the whole, and each cell is ten hundredths of it

writeup.delight: On the fourth phase, the moment Fold is tapped, the ten columns glide together into one long strip, the shaded columns staying shaded, and the per cent card does not change at all.
writeup.opening: Every mount comes up already furnished for its phase with nothing yet typed. On the first phase the full ten by ten grid sits at the left with some columns and cells already shaded deep blue, and the fraction and per cent cards blank. On the second the question card shows a fraction over one hundred beside an empty grid. On the third the grid is empty and the question card asks for a per cent. On the fourth the ten columns of the grid are outlined in amber and the Fold button waits. One thing moves, once: the first cell, or the Fold button on the fourth phase, gives one slow pulse while the voice speaks its opening line, and a finger on it is the whole way in.
writeup.freePlay: Any shading of the grid, scattered or in columns, and the grid folded into its strip and back. Nothing to get right, no target and no timer. The child is left with the same stage and every control unlocked.
writeup.practice: Eight items over the four phases, easy first, on counting out of a hundred, fractions over a hundred, shading a per cent and the strip of ten.

observations.soWhat: any cells of the right count show a per cent.

observations.why: the grid is ten rows deep, and every cell is the same size.
observations.soWhat: counting full columns first, then single cells, makes a count out of a hundred quick.
observations.observe: Every full column held exactly ten cells.

observations.soWhat: a fraction over one hundred is written as a per cent by its numerator.
observations.observe: The numerator on the fraction card and the number on the per cent card were always the same.

observations.why: each column is one tenth of the grid, ten hundredths.
observations.soWhat: each cell of a strip of ten equal cells is ten per cent of the whole.
observations.observe: After folding, one cell of the strip covered what a whole column had.

onWrong.marks: Nothing is marked, nothing resets, no colour means good or bad. The child's answer stays; the pad re-opens after the traceback.
tracebacks: Phase 1: each full shaded column lights amber in turn and the counter adds it, then the single cells; the cards end on the count over 100 and the per cent
Phase 2: the grid shades the top number of cells, full columns first, and the per cent card ends on that number with the % sign
Phase 3: the right count is shaded on a demo layer, full columns first, and the cards end on it; the child's own shading comes back at the next act
Phase 4: each shaded strip cell is labelled with the running per cent in tens, and the cards end on the per cent

voice.rules: Silent: nothing is spoken (no device speech, no recorded clips, no Tap to start cover). The speech bubble is the guide: every instruction and hint is one printed page, numbers as words. The lesson is action-driven in every mode: a guide step's instruction stays until the child does the act it names; a wrong act shows that step's hint under the pinned instruction, a wrong answer the next rung of its ladder, and the hint stays unchanged until the child acts again; a right answer's next question, a phase's next phase and the summary's rows follow by themselves after a short celebration. The header's Hint key shows the step's hint or the next rung on demand. What is heard is sound effects (Web Audio), switched by the sound button, on in every mode. In classroom mode nothing waits for a tap except the pieces of a long line (the blinking arrow; a tap, Enter, Space, ArrowRight or PageDown on the bubble shows the next piece), and a tap on the bubble when nothing waits is the teacher's skip.

guide.playsOn: guide steps on phase 1, 2, 3, 4: the phase opens on its first instruction and waits for the child's act (getState guideStep, guideSteps, guideOn); the agent's check() performs the current step; the last act opens the first question. Other phases open on their printed teach lines, and a demo phase waits for the child's own act.

palette.rule: A content colour fills countable things only and chrome never borrows one; coloured numerals and words take a deeper ink of their colour (4.5:1).

hostContract.phase: absent (not a finite number): the whole lesson, phases one to 4 in a row, the summary page at the end, finished once.
